facts.fact: The study states that since 2002 the Ministry of Health has collected and reported aggregated facility-level data through a unified HMIS under its Central Monitoring and Evaluation Division, which runs on DHIS2 and sets the reporting deadlines; no date is given for the present arrangement, so the document's published date is used.

The study states that as of January 2023, 1,266 health facilities, government-owned, private for-profit and private non-profit, were reporting in the HMIS on DHIS2 (an unpublished figure by its own citation), that some reports exist only at central hospitals, and that all 15 facilities of Neno district report, two hospitals and 13 health centres.

The study states that in practice paper reporting forms are distributed to health facilities, compiled there from programme registers, collected by data clerks and programme coordinators and entered into DHIS2 at the district HMIS office, although in theory any facility with electricity, internet and a computer could report online; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The study states that in November 2022 Neno district began decentralising DHIS2 data entry to its health centres in a step-wedge process; it gives no count of the district's 13 health centres reached.

The study gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports nationally; it finds that yearly median completeness and timeliness of weekly, monthly and quarterly DHIS2 reports rose from 2016 to 2022 at national and South West Zone level but stayed below the 85% national target, Neno district passing it for monthly reports from 2019.

The study states that a DHIS2 system failure occurred in Malawi between March and August 2020, with a substantial drop in monthly report timeliness over those months, and cites a press report of the Ministry of Health losing management data.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health, Central Monitoring and Evaluation Division
systems.tiers: 1,266 facilities, public and private; central hospitals, district and community hospitals, health centres
